findings.title: Header `.panel` right-alignment relies on `margin-left: auto`, which the 2009 `-webkit-box` fallback the mixins emit does not support
findings.body: The new `flexbox()` mixin deliberately emits `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` so that legacy engines (Android 2.x–4.3 stock browser, Safari < 6.1, old Firefox) get a flex layout. However, the header now positions `.panel` on the right solely via `margin-left: auto` (replacing the previous `float: right`). In the 2009 box model, `auto` margins on box children are computed as zero, so in exactly those browsers the fallback is targeting, the panel (user/notification/search icons, login buttons) will collapse to sit immediately after the title/extra-info instead of at the right edge. Previously `float: right` worked everywhere. Either drop the legacy prefixes (so those browsers fall back to normal block flow) or add a 2009-compatible mechanism (e.g. `-webkit-box-pack: justify` on `.contents` or `-webkit-box-flex: 1` on the preceding item).

findings.title: Making `.small-action` a flex container breaks right-alignment of its action buttons
findings.body: `.small-action` is now `display: flex`, but `.small-action-desc` has no `flex: 1`/`flex-grow`, so it shrinks to its content width instead of filling the row as the old block did. The `.small-action button { float: right; }` rule (line 309) therefore either has no effect (if a button is a direct flex child, floats are ignored on flex items) or only floats to the right edge of the now content-sized `.small-action-desc`, placing the edit/delete buttons directly after a short description like "closed 2 hours ago" instead of at the right edge of the post. Add `flex: 1 1 auto` (or `width: 100%`) to `.small-action-desc`, or use `margin-left: auto` on the buttons.

findings.title: `align-items` mixin emits a non-existent `-ms-align-items` property and passes values through unmapped to legacy syntaxes
findings.body: `-ms-align-items` is not a property any IE version ever implemented (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`, IE11 uses unprefixed `align-items`), so line 121 is dead output in every compiled rule that uses the mixin. More importantly, the mixin passes `$alignment` verbatim into `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, which only accept `start`/`end` rather than the modern `flex-start`/`flex-end`; likewise `order()` forwards `$val` into `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`, which requires a positive integer (default 1) while modern `order` defaults to 0 and allows negatives. Today's call sites (`center`, `baseline`, `2`, `3`) happen to be valid in all syntaxes, but the mixins silently produce invalid legacy declarations for any other value, defeating their purpose. Either map values (`flex-start`→`start`, `$val + 1` for ordinal-group) or drop the legacy prefixes.

findings.title: PR title claims a performance optimization; description is a placeholder
findings.body: The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" and described as "Test 5". Nothing in the diff is a performance change: it is a layout refactor replacing float-based positioning of `.title`/`.panel`/`.extra-info-wrapper` and `.small-action` with flexbox, plus new vendor-prefix mixins, with visible rendering consequences (removed margins/paddings, new ordering). The misleading title and empty description will mislead anyone bisecting a header/small-action layout regression later and give reviewers no information about intended visual changes or browser support goals. The title and description should describe the actual change and the browsers the legacy prefixes are meant to support.
